title: Structural abnormalities in the brains of human subjects who use methamphetamine

claims.statement: Structural MRI studies report less grey matter in some frontal, cingulate, insular and temporal regions in people with methamphetamine dependence than in controls, but in the study that separated tobacco smoking, non-using smokers also had less orbitofrontal grey matter than non-smokers, and only 4 of 10 regional differences remained when users were compared with smoking controls. An earlier report of 7.8% smaller hippocampi was not reproduced by the same laboratory, and memory scores were never compared between groups in that report.
claims.magnitude: Thompson et al. (2004; 22 vs 21): cingulate–paralimbic grey matter −11.3%, hippocampus −7.8%, white matter +7.0%. Morales et al. (2012): 10 clusters smaller vs non-smoking controls; 4 vs smoking controls; orbitofrontal smaller in smoking controls too; no dose–response.
